KMS / HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
Audit logs and retention / logging restrictions
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alex (Head of Cloud Security, Sunrise), Priya (Platform), Jared (Compliance), Terry (PM)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm samira from redwood, excited to dig into your compliance needs today. do you want to quickly go around who you are?
[00:08] Alex: yep alex, head of cloud security at sunrise financial, we manage infra across aws and azure, also we have a govcloud presence for some tenants.
[00:14] Priya: priya here, platform lead, we run most services in us-east and eu-west, some on prem for legacy workloads.
[00:20] Jared: jared, compliance - i'll be driving audit and retention requirements.
[00:24] Samira: awesome. quick agenda — understand current stack and constraints, discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private for data residency, list of compliance artifacts you need, and next steps. sound good?
[00:33] Terry: yep, good.

[00:38] Diego: just to add, i'll go through technical tradeoffs on the se side: network isolation, key mgmt, logging, and what our Dedicated and Private options actually give you.

[01:05] Alex: high level — our main ask is: can we ensure customer data (names, account numbers, ssn-ish fields) never leave eu for eu customers, and same for us customers. also we need attestable controls for auditors. we've seen vendors say 'we store regionally' but then logs or backups sneak out.
[01:25] Maya: yes so on redwood hosted, we can pin region at the request/router level, but the distinction is hosted (multi-tenant) vs dedicated pools (isolated GPU pools) vs private (customer-managed control plane).
[01:37] Samira: short answer: hosted can be region-restricted but isn't suitable if you need physical tenancy separation or customer-managed keys. dedicated gives isolated capacity and stronger guarantees; private gives you the full control plane in your VPC/on-prem.

[02:02] Priya: ok can you clarify encryption? we use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys for most services. does redwood allow us to bring our own keys?
[02:12] Diego: we support KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we support provider-managed encryption and we have an option for envelope encryption with a customer key in some enterprise contracts. the stronger model is Private where you control KMS/HSM and keys never transit redwood-managed key stores.
[02:35] Alex: is HSM supported for private? our auditor will want HSM-backed keys for signing.
[02:41] Maya: yes private can be configured to use your HSM/KMS. note: that generally requires on-prem or VPC with KMS endpoints and appropriate network peering.

[03:05] Jared: logging — we have a strict policy. PII may never appear in central logs, and logs that do contain metadata must have retention windows and non-export clauses. how do you handle inference logs, prompts/responses, and KV cache artifacts?
[03:22] Diego: good question. by default hosted logs request/response traces for debugging but we offer redaction at ingest and prefix/KV cache can be configured to not be persisted. for Dedicated you can enable no-persist mode where prompts and outputs are not logged to long-term storage, only metric telemetry. for Private you fully control logs and retention policies.
[03:42] Priya: when you say redaction at ingest — that's automated or we have to supply regex/config? some of our PII patterns are custom.
[03:50] Maya: we support configurable redaction rules (regex) plus a PII detection model option. note transcription sometimes says 'redaction' incorrectly spelled or whatever — sorry bad auto transcribe — but we do have that.

[04:10] Alex: GDPR: we need to know whether data is transferred outside the EU if we use Hosted. what about backups, analytics, and third-party telemetry?
[04:20] Samira: for Hosted we keep region-local storage for primary artifacts, but backups and analytics may be aggregated in central regions unless you opt for Dedicated or Private. for accounts that require EU-only processing we usually recommend Dedicated in EU region or Private deployment. we'll provide Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and SCCs as part of the security pack.

[05:00] Terry: timeline: we want a pilot by end of Q3, production by Q1. we'll need to show auditors evidence of controls during pilot.

[05:12] Diego: pilot options: 1) Hosted region-restricted trial (fastest), 2) Dedicated in EU pool (better isolation and logs configuration), 3) Private in your VPC (slowest to set up but full control). Based on your timeline we can do Dedicated pilot first and migrate to Private later if needed.

[05:32] Priya: cost tradeoffs — Dedicated vs Private differences?
[05:36] Samira: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — monthly commit — more predictable costs; Private has higher setup and infra costs because it's your infra or a single-tenant appliance. We'll send a cost comparison.

[06:10] Alex: auditors will ask for SOC2 and ISO evidence. do you have attestation docs?
[06:15] Samira: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 current reports we can share under NDA. also we can provide architecture diagrams, config checklists, and sample runbooks.

[06:28] Jared: HIPAA? some of our customers are health-adjacent. is redwood willing to sign BAA?
[06:35] Maya: we have a BAA for certain enterprise contracts; Private deployments ease HIPAA compliance since data never leaves your environment. Hosted is possible with contractual protections but tends to be more limited.

[07:00] Priya: network — we need private endpoints, no public internet egress for inference nodes. can you run in our VPC and peer?
[07:08] Diego: Dedicated supports private peering and private endpoints. Private is fully deployed into your VPC or on-prem where inference nodes never touch public internet. for Dedicated there is optional strict egress policies and NAT configurations.

[07:30] Alex: backup and DR — if there is a failover between regions, how do you ensure eu data stays in eu?
[07:38] Samira: cross-region failover is optional — by default we keep regional failover within the same legal boundary, but for hosted failovers some aggregated telemetry can move — again Dedicated/Private give more control. we'll include details in the runbook.

[08:10] Terry: any limitations on model variants if we choose Private? our infra team likes to run open LLMs we already hardened.
[08:18] Maya: Private supports bringing your own models; Dedicated supports curated open models and redwood-verified variants. Hosted has a catalog. Model compat and kernel optimizations vary by hardware — we'll document supported quantization profiles.

[08:45] Jared: audit logs — retention policy, who can access logs, encryption and export controls?
[08:52] Diego: logs are encrypted at rest, access controlled by RBAC. for Dedicated you can choose to send logs to your SIEM over a customer-managed endpoint and set retention. we can implement access control to restrict redwood staff access for Dedicated and Private.

[09:20] Alex: are there any gotchas — things that have tripped other banks?
[09:26] Samira: often it's around metadata leaking in tooling (traces in APM), or backups enabled by default containing prompts. another is key management assumptions — some teams assume provider KMS is same as customer KMS. we recommend explicit runbooks and a pre-deploy security checklist.

[09:58] Priya: what about latency SLAs and fallback models? we might want a lightweight small model that runs on-prem for certain flows.
[10:08] Diego: we support model routing policies — you can route by latency, cost, or region. Private enables running smaller local models; Dedicated supports fallback to smaller variants in the same pool.

[10:35] Terry: ok that's helpful. can you also show an example of redaction and the logs we would get?
[10:40] Maya: yes we'll attach sample logs with redaction applied and an example network diagram and retention config.

[11:00] Samira: quick recap — deliver security pack (SOC2/ISO/DPA), VPC diagram and runbook, proposed pilot scope and pricing for Dedicated EU pool, and schedule SE deep dive next week.
[11:12] Alex: yep, please also note that retention for audit logs is 7 years for certain records — we'll provide the list.

[11:25] Jared: one more — we need proof that logs can't be exported by default, and a technical control to prevent support staff from viewing unredacted prompts.
[11:33] Diego: for Dedicated/Private we can show RBAC controls and implement support access controls and logging for support actions. we'll include an example of our support access policy and how it's logged.

[11:58] Samira: thanks everyone — any final q's?
[12:02] Priya: no, thanks.
[12:05] Terry: all good.

[12:08] Samira: great will send those artifacts. end call.

Notes about transcription: speaker labels sometimes generic, small imperfect transcribe instances (e.g., 'KMS' transcribed as 'K M S' in two places). Timestamps are rough every 30-90 seconds.
